maria-cs: FYI we just got an urgent escalation from Acme — embeddings endpoint showing lots of unexpected misses, latency spike and billing overage. customer says cache hit rate dropped from ~92% to ~3% in last hour :sos:

acme_sre: Confirming. We see a bunch of requests that should hit but end up falling through, then immediate re-compute. Happens on v2 embeddings + tenant prefixing.

ben-support: Can you paste a minimal repro and any logs? Is this only for batched requests or single-item?

acme_sre: Mostly batched calls from our worker. We do 64-item batches, with tenant prefix header `X-Tenant: acme-corp` and model pinned to `openembed-v2`. Repro attached below (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \  -H 'X-Tenant: acme-corp' \  -d '{"model":"openembed-v2","input":["a","b",...]}'
```

sam-eng: Pasted some agent logs from their runs. Notice pattern: the cache proxy logs alternating miss/hit for same logical key within ms. snippet:
```
cache_proxy INFO key=tenant:acme-corp|model:openembed-v2|batch:hash=abc123 miss
cache_proxy INFO key=tenant:acme-corp|model:openembed-v2|batch:hash=abc123 miss
... compute -> store
cache_proxy INFO key=tenant:acme-corp|model:openembed-v2|batch:hash=abc123 hit
```
Seems like two concurrent prefetches racing and one writing a slightly different key (notice subtle `batch:` encoding).

lee-ml: Two hypotheses: 1) prefetcher uses non-normalized prefix (sometimes includes trailing slash or uppercase) which makes two distinct cache keys for same logical tenant. 2) batching code composes batch-level key by concatenating embeddings indices; concurrent workers might produce different ordering leading to different hashes. Both would cause duplicate computes and misleading hit/miss churn.

ben-support: Is it plausible that TTL or eviction is also playing a role? customer reported misses then hits soon after, not long-term eviction.

sam-eng: TTL seems fine. The pattern looks like a race + inconsistent key normalization. Also saw one log where `Content-Length` header trimmed in proxy, which affects the batching canonicalization.

kaya-eng-runtime: Reproduced locally with a small harness. If you send 2 simultaneous identical batch requests with slight header order diff, you can get two different cache keys. Repro steps I used: run two parallel `curl` with the same body but different `Accept` header order. Will push a short test to the infra repo.

maria-cs: Acme is requesting immediate mitigation — they want either: (A) disable prefetch for tenant acme-corp, or (B) a quick config to force normalized tenant-keying.

kaya-eng-runtime: For immediate mitigation I can flip the `prefetch.enable` flag for that tenant from our control plane and throttle prefetch rate. That should cut down the thundering-prefetch. I'll do that once we confirm tenant id. :lock:

lee-ml: Longer term fix: unify cache key canonicalization in proxy (normalize tenant header, canonicalize header ordering & body whitespace, and switch to stable hash of canonicalized JSON for batches). I'll raise a PR with test vectors (ordering, header variation, unicode normalization).

ben-support: Customer asked for why costs spiked. Can we estimate extra token/embed compute?

sam-eng: From their logs approx +18k extra vector computes in the hour window — we should prepare an invoice adjustment proposal. cc @maria-cs.

cachebot: deploy:prefetch-patch candidate built by kaya-eng-runtime — CI green, staging tested at 10k req/s with deterministic keys.

kaya-eng-runtime: Plan: 1) flip off prefetch for acme-corp now; 2) deploy canonicalization patch to canary tonight; 3) monitor hit rate and rollback if regressions. I'll open an incident ticket and assign priority P1.

maria-cs: Please add Acme SRE to ticket and include sample logs + suggested credit. I'll send them the mitigation steps now. :white_check_mark:

ben-support: Thx all. Next actions: kaya to flip flag + open ticket; lee to open PR and include test vectors; sam to prepare cost delta. I'll draft customer-facing summary for Maria to send.

acme_sre: Thanks team — mitigation looks good. We appreciate the quick response. We'll wait for follow-up on root cause and billing adj.

kaya-eng-runtime: Flag flipped for acme-corp (prefetch disabled). Observability: hit-rate jumped from 3% -> 86% within 90s. Rolling canary will include canonicalizer changes.

ben-support: Adding note for billing: log window 2023-06-21T18:12:00Z -> 2023-06-21T19:15:00Z shows excess computes. Maria, attach that to the customer credit request.

maria-cs: On it. Will also schedule a postmortem with Acme next week.

sam-eng: For engineering follow-up I'll record the reproducer and add a small harness in `infra/tests/cache_key_repro` so we don't regress.

lee-ml: Also adding a unit test for batch-key stability with shuffled headers and body whitespace variants.

ben-support: Great. Closing loop here — mark this thread resolved unless new info appears. :thumbsup:
